C005.subject: Artificial general intelligence (AGI)
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Artificial general intelligence (AGI) 10 years]

[PATH:empirical] Long-term trend analysis of AI capability benchmarks (e.g., ARC-AGI, MMLU, or similar) combined with compute scaling laws — If progress on key AGI-relevant benchmarks continues to follow a predictable scaling curve without sudden jumps, it would suggest that a major architectural breakthrough is unlikely within 5 years, refuting the conditional hypothesis. Conversely, a sudden acceleration would support it.

[PATH:literature] Survey of leading AI labs' published roadmaps and open-source projects on recursive self-improvement architectures (e.g., meta-learning, self-play, automated architecture search) — A systematic review of current R&D efforts can reveal whether the field is actively pursuing or already demonstrating the required breakthrough, helping to assess the plausibility of the condition being met within the 5-year window.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of the feasibility and safety constraints of recursive self-improvement, drawing on formal results in machine learning theory and AI alignment literature — If rigorous mathematical arguments show that recursive self-improvement is fundamentally limited by computational or logical barriers (e.g., no-free-lunch theorems, impossibility of stable self-modification), then the hypothesis's condition is unlikely to be met, refuting the overall claim.

scope.domain: only if a major architectural breakthrough (e.g., recursive self-improvement) occurs within the next 5 years

qualifier.temporal: starting from 2025, conditional on a major architectural breakthrough within the next 5 years

C006.subject: Artificial general intelligence (AGI)
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Artificial general intelligence (AGI) 20 years]

[PATH:empirical] Long-term trend analysis of AI capability benchmarks (e.g., MMLU, ARC, BIG-bench) and compute scaling laws (e.g., from Epoch AI or Open Philanthropy projects) — Tracking historical rates of improvement on diverse cognitive tasks and extrapolating scaling trends (compute, data, algorithmic efficiency) can provide empirical evidence for or against reaching AGI within 20 years.

[PATH:literature] Survey of expert forecasts on AGI timelines (e.g., from AI Impacts, Müller & Bostock, or recent 2023-2025 Delphi studies) — Systematic aggregation of expert opinions (e.g., median predicted year of AGI) and analysis of calibration accuracy over time can confirm or refute the plausibility of a 20-year timeline.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of fundamental limits in AI (e.g., computational complexity, resource constraints, or arguments from neuroscience about required brain-scale simulation) — Identifying necessary conditions for AGI (e.g., specific algorithmic breakthroughs or hardware requirements) and assessing whether they are achievable within 20 years provides a theoretical basis to evaluate the hypothesis.

scope.domain: mainstream AI research with sustained funding

C007.subject: Artificial general intelligence (AGI)
C007.object: the development of a unified theory of cortical computation and its successful hardware emulation
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Artificial general intelligence (AGI) the development of a unified theory of cortical computation and its successful hardware emulation]

[PATH:literature] Systematic review of cortical computation theories (e.g., predictive coding, hierarchical temporal memory, Bayesian brain) and their implementation in neuromorphic hardware platforms (e.g., Intel Loihi, IBM TrueNorth) — Evaluates whether existing partial cortical theories, when implemented in hardware, produce AGI-like capabilities, thus testing the necessity of a unified theory.

[PATH:empirical] Controlled experiments comparing AGI performance metrics (e.g., generalization, transfer learning, autonomy) between systems based on unified cortical emulation vs. alternative architectures (e.g., large-scale transformer models, reinforcement learning agents) — Directly tests the causal claim by measuring whether unified cortical emulation yields superior AGI performance relative to non-cortical approaches.

[PATH:theoretical] Formal analysis of computational complexity and resource requirements for scaling current partial cortical models to AGI-level tasks, with and without a unified theory — Determines whether a unified theory is logically or computationally necessary for AGI, or whether incremental integration of partial models could suffice.

qualifier.temporal: until a unified theory of cortical computation is developed and successfully emulated in hardware

C008.subject: Artificial general intelligence (AGI)
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Artificial general intelligence (AGI) 10 years or less]

[PATH:empirical] Tracking of AI benchmark saturation rates (e.g., MMLU, BIG-bench, and agentic tasks) over the next 5 years — Rapid saturation of multiple diverse benchmarks would indicate accelerating progress toward AGI, while stagnation or slowdown would refute the 10-year timeline.

[PATH:theoretical] Meta-analysis of historical AI capability scaling laws (compute, data, model size) and their projected extrapolation to human-level performance — If scaling trends predict reaching human-level capabilities within 10 years, this supports the hypothesis; if diminishing returns or theoretical limits are observed, it refutes it.

[PATH:literature] Systematic literature review of expert surveys and Delphi studies on AGI timelines (e.g., from AI Impacts, 2022-2025 updates) — Consensus or shift in expert predictions toward a 10-year horizon would confirm the hypothesis; persistent longer median estimates would refute it.

scope.domain: optimistic AI development and technological acceleration perspectives

C011.subject: Artificial general intelligence (AGI)
C011.object: a fundamentally new cognitive architecture inspired by biological neural plasticity is developed
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Artificial general intelligence (AGI) a fundamentally new cognitive architecture inspired by biological neural plasticity is developed]

[PATH:empirical] Long-term experimental studies on neuromorphic chips with real-time synaptic plasticity (e.g., Intel Loihi or IBM TrueNorth) applied to open-ended learning tasks — Directly tests whether architectures inspired by biological neural plasticity can achieve general intelligence benchmarks; failure would refute the hypothesis, while success would support it.

[PATH:theoretical] Comparative analysis of AGI performance between current deep learning architectures and those incorporating Hebbian plasticity, spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP), and structural plasticity in simulated environments (e.g., OpenAI Gym or Meta-World) — Provides a controlled theoretical test of whether plasticity-based designs are necessary for AGI-level generalization and adaptation, isolating the causal role of biological inspiration.

[PATH:literature] Systematic review of evolutionary biology and neuroscience literature on the specific computational roles of neural plasticity in animal cognition (e.g., work by Jeff Hawkins, Karl Friston, or the Blue Brain Project) — Evaluates whether the hypothesized necessity of plasticity for general intelligence is consistent with known biological constraints and evolutionary evidence, potentially confirming or refuting the assumption that such architectures are indispensable.
